summary: You choose the coterminal MA or the MA. Coterminal: SOC 270 and 280A and 45 units at the 100 level or above, at least 23 at the 200 level, with at most 12 units in the SOC 290 series (5 of them SOC 290) and 5 from other social science departments. MA: 45 units of Sociology, up to 15 of them petitioned flex units from elsewhere. Both are letter graded. Your 3.0 GPA, advance approval of outside courses, a research-track student's 18 units in the 290 series and the rule that workshops and colloquia do not count are checked by hand.

program.why: Coterminal: "All units applied to the coterminal master's degree must be taken for a letter grade". MA: "All courses must be taken for a letter grade when possible."

totals.label: SOC 290 series (SOC 290, 291, 292)
totals.why: Coterminal: "Coterminal master's students are limited to five units from other Social Sciences departments (Anthropology, Communications, Economics, Political Science and Psychology). Up to five units can be taken as an independent study or directed reading (SOC 290 Coterminal MA individual study) with a faculty member appointed in Sociology, but no more than 12 units of coursework across the 290 series (including SOC 291, SOC 292) can be counted toward the degree." The 290 series is SOC 290, 291 and 292 (SOC 297 and 298 are ordinary courses). A research-track student's 18 units ("Student in the research track can count up to 18 units across the SOC 290 series") are moved in by hand. The caps cover the whole degree, not each rule.

children.name: Core Course Requirements
children.notes: All coterminal students are required to take course Classics of Modern Social Theory and course Foundations of Social Research (or their 100-level counterparts if taken previously as a Sociology BA). These introductory theory and methods courses are essential to graduate training in the social sciences.
